correctness.rationale: Length-1 observations give symbol totals; length-2 homogeneous pairs recover run counts; length-3 homogeneous triples recover singleton runs; mixed triples recover the endpoint statistic e. Conversely the seven-number signature reconstructs every observed count. Endpoint options for balanced and imbalanced run counts are classified exhaustively, feasible run lengths have exact positive-composition support series, and geometric summation establishes the stated rational function. The leading Laurent coefficient is 3/4 at the fifth-order pole z=1, producing n^4/32. Literal enumeration through 16, structurally independent feasible-signature enumeration through 20, and bitwise dynamic programming through 38 agree with direct rational coefficient recurrence. Infinite proof does not rely on experiments.

value.rationale: This is the natural maximal number of perfectly distinguishable binary codewords when a polymer readout gives compositions for every length up to three. It determines an entire infinite family, with exact rational/quasipolynomial counts and asymptotic n^4/32, and exposes an endpoint-run statistic genuinely absent from the earlier quadratic limit-two result. It is not a one-off finite experiment or a trivial renaming, and the precise capacity is required for benchmark coding bounds.
